concept.name: Automatic reaction
concept.definition: The Wyckoff event (AR) in distribution in which price falls sharply after a buying climax because intense buying has been exhausted while heavy supply continues. Its low helps define the lower boundary of the distribution trading range.
concept.intuition: Once the euphoric buyers are spent, the price drops on its own weight — no extra selling pressure needed.
concept.mechanics: After the buying climax fills urgent public demand, the withdrawal of bids lets price decline quickly; the AR low, together with the climax high and subsequent secondary tests, sets the boundaries of the distribution range that the analyst uses for later labeling.
concept.failure_modes: The reaction is 'automatic' and can be brief; in a continuing bull market the dip is bought and the advance resumes, so an AR alone does not establish a top.
concept.misconceptions: The automatic reaction is not yet proof of distribution; it reflects exhausted buyers more than committed sellers, and its significance comes only from the range that develops around it.
concept.example: After a climax spike to 150 on record volume, a stock sinks to 136 within days on much lighter buying; the analyst draws the bottom of the developing distribution range near 136.

citations.source: The Wyckoff Method: A Tutorial (StockCharts.com ChartSchool, by Roman Bogomazov and Michael Lipsett)
